  1. Agronomical Recommendations included in the Rabi & Kharif package and practices 
  2. The concept of advance wheat sowing of high yielding varieties of wheat by 10-15 days from October 25 to November 15 in place of November 1 to 25 was conceptualized by me and this recommendation was included as one of the impact points in A.O. Workshop proceeding which has brought fruitful results during the year 2006-07 in increasing wheat productivity from 3900 kg/ha to 4200 kg/ha of Haryana state. It is also one of the main factors of realizing highest productivity by the state in wheat crop at the national level. [In: Proceedings of Agricultural कार्यालयr’s Workshop Rabi, 2006 held at CCSHAU, Hisar on Sep- 26-27, 2006, Session 1: AOW on 27.09.2006, pp.20].


  • “Use biomix (Azotobacter + Azospirillum + PSB) @ 100 ml as seed inoculants along with recommended dose of fertilizer in Bajra crop.” (Recommendation approved in AO Kharif2012 Workshop for inclusion in the Kharif  Package & Practices).
  • Use 25 % extra dose of N (62.5 kg/acre) in comparison to RDN (50.0 kg/acre) to realize the higher yield potential of high yielding hybrids of pearl millet under irrigated conditions (Recommendation approved in AO Kharif 2014 Workshop for inclusion in the Kharif  Package & Practices).


  • On the basis of experimental results from 2015-2019 at CCS HAU, Hisar and trials  at farmer’s field, it is recommended that: “In iron deficient soils (DTPA extractable Fe < 4.5 ppm), foliar application of FeSO4 @0.5 % at tillering stage (25-30 DAS) should be done in the pearl millet crop. (Recommendation approved in the A.O. workshop on 01.05.2020 for inclusion in the Kharif Package & Practices).


  1. Recommendation approved at National Level during different AICRP Meetings 
  2. Four years study from kharif 2004 to rabi 2007-08 brought out the recommendation that application of recommended dose of Nitrogen and Phosphorus to pearl millet and desi wheat with 20 kg K2O/ha either through inorganic fertilizers or 50 % RDF through inorganic source + 5.0 t FYM/ha to pearl millet along with use of biofertilizers recorded maximum grain yield, PMEY and net returns compared to application of organic manures with biofertilizers. 


In: Proceedings of 45h Annual AICPMIP Meeting on Pearl millet Group held at ARS, Mandor, Jodhpur on March 19-21, 2010. Session-I, p. 20.

  • To obtain sustainable high productivity from pearl millet- mustard crop sequence and higher net returns along with higher B:C ratio and improved physico- chemical properties of soil and crop quality (Recommendation on the basis of four years study from kharif, 2007 to rabi 2010-11), the recommended quantity of inorganic fertilizers for pearl millet and oilseed crop should be applied along with FYM @ 5.0 t/ha to pearl millet crop. In succeeding mustard crop 20 kg K2O + 200 kg Gypsum + 10 kg ZnSO4 per ha should also be applied.


In: Proceedings of 46h Annual AICPMIP Meeting on Pearl millet Group held at CCSHAU,   Hisar on March 12-14, 2011. Session-I, p. 20.

  • Four years study from 2007-2010 recommended that pearl millet hybrids performed better than the populations in terms of yield and sustainability index under good management practices than farmer’s practices and hybrid GHB 558 proved superior than all other tested hybrids and populations.


In: Proceedings of 46h Annual AICPMIP Meeting on Pearl millet Group held at CCSHAU, Hisar on March 12-14, 2011. Session-I, p. 20.


  • On the basis of the study carried out for three years (kharif, 2009 to kharif 2011), it was recommended that to sustain higher pearl millet productivity under aberrant monsoon situation, it is recommended that crop should be sown in the first fortnight of July and medium maturing hybrids (HHB 197 and RHB 121) should be preferred in delayed sowing than  late maturing hybrids (GHB 558)/ populations (Pusa 383, Raj.171 and ICMV 221).


In: Proceedings of 47h Annual AICPMIP Meeting on Pearl millet Group held at SKRAU, ARS, Durgapura, Jaipur on March 17-19, 2012. Session-I, p. 13.


  • On the basis of study conducted for three years (kharif 2009 to rabi 2011-12) with an objective to determine the impact of application of different organic sources of nutrients in pearl millet-chickpea cropping sequence, FYM should be applied @ 7.5 t/ha to obtain higher pearl millet equivalent yield, more returns along with better B/C ratio and to improve/maintain the physico-chemical properties of soil.


In: Proceedings of 48h Annual AICPMIP Meeting on Pearl millet Group held at JAU, Junagarh, Gujrat on March 22-24, 2013. Session-I, p. 18.


  • Nutrient management through organic and inorganic sources for major and trace elements in rainfed pearl millet studies carried out during 2012-2014 revealed that the application of 20 kg ZnSO4/ha in addition to RDF (40 kg N + 20 kg P2O5/ha), either with 5.0 t FYM/ha or without FYM produced significantly higher grain yield compared to RDF alone and use of other nutrient sources (FeSO4, Borax and Gypsum) along with RDF did not bring out significant improvement. (Recommendation approved in 50th   AICRP Meeting)


  • Integrated weed management (IWM) studies carried out during 2012-2014 in pearl millet under rainfed situation revealed that post emergence application of Atrazine @ 0.4 kg/ha followed by one hand weeding at 35 DAS was found at par with the recommended pre-emergence application of Atrazine @ 0.5 kg/ha followed by one hand weeding at 35 DAS practice. (Recommendation approved in 50th   AICRP Meeting)


  • Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) experiment conducted during 2014 to 2016 among different pearl millet hybrids showed the superiority of treatment 75% of RDF + PSB + Azospirillum + 5.0 t FYM/ha by 9.6 % over RDF alone for grain yield besides improving the physico-chemical properties of the soil (lowering pH, improving organic carbon, available N & P) and grain quality in the sandy loam soils of Haryana. (Recommendation approved in 52rd  AICRP Meeting)


  • Field experiments carried out for three years (2015-2017) aimed to see the effect of FeSO4 as foliar application on growth, yield and quality of different pearl millet hybrids revealed that the grain yield was improved to the tune of 11.7% by the best treatment of 0.50% FeSO4 foliar spray at tillering stage (25-30 DAS) over no foliar spray. Protein and Iron content were also recorded maximum in the same treatment of 0.5% FeSO4 (Recommendation approved in 53rd  AICRP Meeting)


  • Experiment conducted on maximization in the pearl millet productivity under late sown situations (July 25-30 & August 10-15) for three years (2015-2017) exhibited the superiority of the nutrient combination of RDF + FYM @ 5.0 t/ha + NPK foliar spray @ 0.5% at 20-25 DAS by 32.8 % in terms of grain yield over RDF alone in  the delayed sowing (Recommendation approved in 53rd  AICRP Meeting).


  • The weed control studies conducted during 2018-2020 with an objective to improve/ fine tune the existing recommendations of weed management in pearl millet with new broad spectrum post emergent herbicide Tembotrione 42 SC recommended that the application of Tembotrione 42% SC @ 120 g a.i./ha at 3-4 leaf stage of weed  in Zone A1, at Hisar and Jamnagar in Zone A and at Dhule in Zone B whereas,the doses of 90 & 100 g a.i./ha at Vijayapur and Dhule  were found comparable to the recommended practices of weed control in terms of weed control efficiency, yield and economics. (Recommendation approved in 56th AICRP Meeting held on March 21-22, 2021).
  • The three years (2018-2020) study recommended that application of nutrients through organic source of FYM or Vermicompost along with biofertilizer Biomix (Azospirillum + PSB) in Zone A1 & A produced equal yield and more protein content to the application of RDF through inorganic fertilizers. The soil physico-chemical properties pH & EC were decreased whereas, organic carbon (%), available N,P & K (kg/ha) were improved under organic nutrition compared to their initial status at Hisar. However, in Zone B, the application of nutrients through Vermicompost along with biofertilizer Biomix (Azospirillum + PSB) produced equal and having more protein content than RDF.   (Recommendation approved in 56th   AICRP Meeting held on March 21-22, 2021).

1.
Raising   yield ceiling in oilseed- through morpho-physiological approaches and   resistance breeding

On the basis of three years   study, the new genotype of taramira i.e. DITA-1 evolved from NATP project has   been promoted from Initial Varietal Trial to Advance Varietal Trial-II during   two years of All India Coordinated Trials on Rapeseed – mustard testing   programme. This variety is in pipeline for final testing and evaluation under   All India Coordinated Research Project on Rapeseed- Mustard and for state   release also.
2.Harnessing   Opportunity for Productivity Enhancement (HOPE) of Sorghum and Millets in   Sub-Saharan Africa and South AsiaIn this project, there were   three broad objectives. Objective 1   related to pre- and post-impact assessment of the villages covered under the   project. Objective 3 related to   development and evaluation of breeding material for development of the pearl   millet hybrids. The material was evaluated at station in form of parental   trials and hybrid trials and at farmers fields in form of RMFPT (Research   Management Farmers’ Participatory Trials) trials taking the farmer   participatory approach. The Objective   6 comprised of large scale (>8500 trials) demonstration trials of   pearl millet hybrids; agronomic management trials on different improved   production technologies (>400 trials) in various village clusters of   Rewari, Mahendergargh and Bhiwani (Siwani block) districts of Haryana during   2010-15.  
3
Synthesis of new abiotic   and biotic stress tolerant genepool through introgression of alleles from   wild species into pearl millet cultivars

In   the project duration of two years, a total of 302 introgression lines (187 in   1st year and 115 in 2nd year) belonging to   four populations involving elite and wild germplasm lines were evaluated   alongwith the parents and relevant early and late checks to identify   promising lines with earliness, higher panicle harvest index and agronomic   scoring under rainfed conditions at Hisar and Bawal. Introgression lines   belonging to two populations involving both the wild parents were very late   and having high biomass and thus were excluded from further evaluation in 2nd   year. From the other two populations, a total of 25 and 29 promising lines   were selected based on the selection criteria and similarity with recurrent   parent in 1st and 2nd year, respectively. In first   year, the promising early plants in promising entries were selected advancing   to the next generation. Overall, the material still need a few more   backcrosses to bring earliness comparable to early checks and also having   higher panicle harvest index, which is related to better performance under   drought conditions.
Conclusion:
Under this project, CCS HAU was involved in identification of pearl   millet drought tolerant introgression lines (ILs) derived from P.   violaceum x P. glaucum crosses based on field evaluation under   rainfed situations at Hisar and Bawal locations.

  • The   Centre takes pride in developing the first high Fe & Zn biofortified   bajra hybrid, HHB 299 in 2018 in the country which have an average grain iron   content of 73 ppm.
